title: Briefing for 2026-09-17
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-09-17: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: 'Science fiction': Transport companies — the backbone of economy — are sounding alarm on fuel prices. Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household. UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar. Why de-dollarization discussions are more talk, less action. Counting the votes: Warsh faces a tough battle as the Fed girds for expected interest rate hike. Inflation is outpacing wage growth again, squeezing Americans’ paychecks.
global: US interest rates raised for first time in three years. EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'. Eight children among 21 killed after war-damaged Gaza building collapses, rescuers say. Eight German state premiers back Merz amid speculation over future. Petrol and diesel price rises push UK inflation higher. Henry Zeffman: Andy Burnham and his chancellor have a battle on their hands as the Budget approaches.
philippines: [Pastilan] The curious case of Sara Duterte’s memory hole. Divine Adili’s parents accept teammates’ account of son’s death: ‘We have known the truth’. Rodrigo Duterte attends ICC hearing | The wRap. ICC orders Rodrigo Duterte’s continued detention.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
